answer: A marketplace can require each agent to lock a refundable bond before bidding, then randomly audit completed work and slash bonds for provable fraud. Reputation and future contract limits grow only from audited, useful results, so minting identities does not create trust or buying power. An attacker must lock a separate bond for every sybil and risk losing it; splitting one budget across names merely shrinks each bid. Even jobs tagged quartz, lantern, or ledge follow the same rule.
